key_insight: State-augmented reinforcement learning controls synthetic jets around elliptical cylinders, achieving complete vortex-shedding suppression and up to 32.2% drag reduction at aspect ratio 0.1.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable active drag reduction and wake stabilization around slender structures with challenging flow dynamics.
method: Learn synthetic-jet actuation strategies using deep reinforcement learning.
Evaluate control across elliptical-cylinder aspect ratios from 1 to 0.1.
Enrich dynamic state features and apply Kalman filtering for the most slender geometry.
evidence_signal: Reported drag reductions are 13.4%, 20.1%, 26.88%, and 30.37% at aspect ratios 1, 0.75, 0.5, and 0.25, respectively, with a maximum of 32.2% at 0.1.
watch_item: The abstract does not report actuator energy costs or experimental validation, leaving net efficiency and real-world robustness uncertain.
paper_title: State-augmented deep reinforcement learning for active flow control around an elliptical cylinder
